title: Geometric Meaning of Zeros

hero.headline: Zeros & Graphs
hero.subtext: Where the graph meets the x-axis

story.text: The zeros of a polynomial are the x-coordinates where its graph intersects the x-axis. Let's explore the beautiful connection between algebra and geometry!

explanation.content: For a polynomial y = p(x), the zeros are the points where y = 0, i.e., where the graph crosses or touches the x-axis.
Zero = x-intercept of the graph
Linear polynomial (degree 1): Graph is a straight line → 1 zero
Quadratic polynomial (degree 2): Graph is a parabola → up to 2 zeros
Cubic polynomial (degree 3): Graph has up to 3 zeros
💡 Number of real zeros ≤ Degree of polynomial
A linear polynomial p(x) = ax + b (where a ≠ 0) has exactly one zero.
Graph: A straight line
Zero: x = -b/a (where line crosses x-axis)
Example: p(x) = 2x - 4 → Zero at x = 2
The line always crosses the x-axis at exactly one point
A quadratic polynomial p(x) = ax² + bx + c (where a ≠ 0) has a parabola as its graph. The number of zeros depends on where the parabola meets the x-axis.
Case 1: Parabola cuts x-axis at 2 points → 2 distinct real zeros
Case 2: Parabola touches x-axis at 1 point → 1 repeated real zero
Case 3: Parabola doesn't meet x-axis → No real zeros (complex zeros)
Discriminant (D) decides the number of zeros:
D = b² - 4ac
For quadratic ax² + bx + c = 0:

D > 0 → 2 distinct real zeros
D = 0 → 1 repeated real zero
D < 0 → No real zeros (complex)
A cubic polynomial p(x) = ax³ + bx² + cx + d can have 1, 2, or 3 real zeros.
3 real zeros: Graph crosses x-axis at 3 points
1 real + 2 complex zeros: Graph crosses x-axis at 1 point only
2 real zeros (one repeated): Graph crosses and touches x-axis
Shape: Like a 'wave' or 'S' curve

questions.question: A quadratic polynomial can have at most how many real zeros?
questions.explanation: Quadratic polynomial ki degree 2 hoti hai. Maximum real zeros = degree = 2.

questions.question: If the graph of p(x) does not intersect the x-axis, then:
questions.explanation: Graph x-axis ko na chhune ka matlab: no real zeros. Lekin complex zeros hamesha exist karte hain (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).

questions.question: For x² - 6x + 9 = 0, the discriminant D is:
questions.explanation: D = b² - 4ac = (-6)² - 4(1)(9) = 36 - 36 = 0. Isliye 1 repeated real zero hoga.

questions.question: A linear polynomial always has exactly one real zero.
questions.explanation: True! Linear polynomial ax + b = 0 ka hamesha ek hi solution hota hai: x = -b/a.

questions.question: If D < 0 for a quadratic, the graph:
questions.explanation: D < 0 means no real roots, isliye graph x-axis ko kabhi nahi milega.

notes: Zero = x-coordinate where graph meets x-axis
Quadratic (degree 2): 0, 1, or 2 real zeros (depends on D = b² - 4ac)
Number of real zeros can never exceed the degree
If D > 0: 2 zeros, D = 0: 1 zero, D < 0: No real zeros
summary: Key Points to Remember. Zero = x-coordinate where graph meets x-axis Linear (degree 1): Always 1 real zero
